columns.label: Ebook
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily get and consume ebooks on the platform (free or paid) as a first-class product, open, buy, borrow, or read without hunting.

columns.label: Short-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily consume short-form video as a first-class surface (For You, Reels, Shorts).

columns.label: Long-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch creator / UGC long-form video (or specialty long video) as a core surface. Course lectures belong under Courses. Hollywood catalogs belong under Series/Films.

columns.label: Series/Films
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch series and films as an SVOD / catalog entertainment product.

columns.label: Courses
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily take or browse structured courses as a first-class product.

columns.label: Newsletters
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily read or subscribe to newsletters / creator writing as a first-class product.

columns.label: Audio
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily listen to music, podcasts, or audiobooks as a first-class product.

columns.label: Memberships
columns.definition: Yes if a creator or seller can accept payments from others and make money through the platform, checkout, fan subscriptions, tips, ads, shop, or creator funds. Not only a classic Patreon-style membership product.

columns.label: Community & Messaging
columns.definition: Yes if you can create or join a group, community, or club, including group chats, Groups, subreddits, community tabs, discussion boards, or community feeds. A one-off comment on a single video or listing is not the bar; a durable place for the group to talk is.

columns.label: Storefronts
columns.definition: Yes if the product gives a creator a custom storefront or site that can take the place of building their own website (bio page, creator site, branded shop). Not a shop tab on someone else’s multi-seller marketplace.

columns.label: Marketplaces
columns.definition: Yes if a typical person can search and shop a catalog of offerings from many sellers, courses, books, digital goods, etc. Storefront software (Shopify, WooCommerce) is not a marketplace unless shoppers browse many sellers there.

scaleFacts: Part of Nas Company (Nas Daily, Nas.com, Nas House, etc.), ecosystem reaching ≈300M people globally each month.
Materials cite 200K+ users building digital businesses and ≈350K people across 150+ countries selling on Nas.com.

Positioned as the “fastest way to build a digital business using AI”, memberships, courses, events, challenges, storefront/checkout (Stripe), AI ideation, email/marketing automation, WhatsApp/Discord/Telegram integrations.
Pricing: Free Basic USD 0/mo with ≈7.9% transaction fee; Pro ≈USD 29–30/mo with ≈4.9% fee and priority support, no upfront cost; pay when you sell.

strengths.title: All-in-one creator business stack
strengths.detail: Community, memberships, courses, events, digital products, and marketing automation in one place, less multi-tool sprawl.

strengths.title: AI-powered launch and marketing
strengths.detail: AI suggests offers from social presence, helps ideate products, and automates content, ads, upsells, and abandoned-cart flows.

strengths.title: Community-first on existing chat apps
strengths.detail: Monetization layered over WhatsApp, Discord, and Telegram, communities stay where members already are.

strengths.title: Low barrier to entry and global payments
strengths.detail: Free basic plan and simple setup (describe offer + photo); worldwide payments with clear revenue tracking.

weaknesses.title: Transaction-fee heavy model at scale
weaknesses.detail: ≈7.9% (Basic) / ≈4.9% (Pro) can feel expensive vs low-fee gateways or fixed-fee platforms for high-revenue creators.

weaknesses.title: Complex product surface for new users
weaknesses.detail: AI, communities, courses, events, storefronts, and campaigns can overwhelm beginners with a simple product to sell.

weaknesses.title: Still emerging vs incumbents
weaknesses.detail: Competes with Kajabi, Circle, Patreon, Shopify, etc., ecosystem and tutorials are growing but smaller.

weaknesses.title: Reliance on external messaging apps
weaknesses.detail: Deep WhatsApp/Discord/Telegram ties mean UX and retention partly depend on those platforms.

content:
Kahana is a library of curated hubs, Explore, Clubs, and optional Stripe. Nas.io / Nas.com is aI-powered platform for creators to launch and monetize communities, memberships, courses, events, and digital products, often layered on WhatsApp, Discord, and Telegram. They overlap in places and diverge in others.

What each one is

Kahana is built around hubs people can open, Explore so strangers can find them, Aura as scarce daily recognition, and Clubs so discussion outlives a feed. Selling stays optional.

Nas. Official site.

Why this comparison

This article puts Kahana and Nas.io / Nas.com side by side. It covers what each supports as a first-class product job, key features, and a few research notes so you have a clearer picture of what they are, how they compare, and what you can actually do on each one. It is not a teardown, and it is not a switch-tomorrow pitch.
contentAfter:
What you can do on each

On Kahana you can publish a hub, list it on Explore, discuss it in a Club, grant Aura, and turn on a Stripe paywall when you are ready to charge.

On Nas.io / Nas.com you can use Courses, Memberships, Community & Messaging, and Storefronts as first-class product jobs. The job is hanging out, announcements, and live conversation, not packaging knowledge into something strangers can browse later.

Using Kahana with Nas.io / Nas.com

You can use both. Nas.io / Nas.com keeps doing what it already does well. Kahana is another place to package the work, get discovered, and grow an audience.

Keep live conversation on Nas.io / Nas.com. Pin a Kahana hub or Club link in a channel, discuss live there, and assign the next ebook, video, or course from Kahana so the syllabus is not buried in the thread.
